title: Introduction to Mass Communication

Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: Mass communication is 'public communication transmitted ______ or ______'.
State true or false: (i) The telegraph was invented by Samuel Morse in 1835. (ii) Television started in India in 1959.
Match: (i) Paper (ii) Gutenberg (iii) Marconi (iv) Baird with (a) radio (b) television (c) printing (d) papyrus.
Fill in the blanks: Mahatma Gandhi started ______ in South Africa in 1903 and wrote for ______ in India.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: How can we define mass communication in the simplest way?
questions.answer: Mass communication is public communication transmitted electronically or mechanically to a large audience through the mass media.

questions.q: Describe any two forms of mass media with examples.
questions.answer: Newspapers inform people of events and views, e.g. daily newspapers; television gives audio-visual programmes, e.g. news and serials on Doordarshan.

questions.q: Name the three functions of mass media with one example each.
questions.answer: Inform – news bulletin; educate – a doctor's talk on preventing disease; entertain – films and serials.

questions.q: What is convergence?
questions.answer: The coming together of many forms of media and formats such as printed text, photographs, films, radio and television in new media.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Define mass communication and its process with 'channel of communication' using a flow diagram.
questions.answer: Mass communication is public communication transmitted electronically or mechanically. Process: Communicator (who) → Message (says what) → Channel (newspaper, radio, TV) → Receiver (to whom) → Effect (with what effect), with feedback from the receiver.

questions.q: Explain the functions of mass communication.
questions.answer: It informs through news, educates through talks and campaigns (Green Revolution, polio), and entertains through films, serials and music.

questions.q: Describe the origin of mass communication.
questions.answer: From horse messengers and pigeons to paper, printing (Gutenberg), telegraph (Morse 1835), telephone (Bell 1876), radio (Marconi 1901), transistor (1947) and television (Baird 1920).

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain briefly the different forms of mass media.
questions.answer: Newspapers and journalism, wireless communication, photography, films, radio, television, new media with convergence, and traditional media such as folk songs, street theatre and puppetry; each reaches large audiences in its own way.

questions.q: Describe the functions and origin of mass communication.
questions.answer: Functions: inform, educate, entertain, and bring effect. Origin: invention of paper and printing, newspapers, telegraph, telephone, radio, transistor, television; it developed fully in the 20th century.
